Other words

  • mercimōnium, mercimōniī n. — goods, wares

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. prol. 1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 130: deal, mercimōnium

    Lewis & Short gives only “goods, wares, merchandise” (Plautus and post-Augustan prose); Traupman’s “deal” is not its sense.

  • vēnālīcia, vēnālīciōrum n. pl. — merchandise

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · modern · Traupman 131

    The adjective vēnālīcius, “for sale”, is classical (Petr.); the neuter plural as “merchandise” is Traupman’s. In Suetonius and Pliny it mostly concerns the slave trade.

See also shop, sell, supermarket.
